TrailGuard — Privacy-Preserving, Explainable Insider-Threat Detection on IBM LinuxONE

Privacy-preserving, explainable insider-threat detection — running entirely on IBM LinuxONE.

See the pipelineOpen dashboard
logs→pseudonymize→features→hybrid models→risk + reasons→policy tier→analyst

The goal in one sentence

Build an insider-threat detection pipeline that runs entirely on LinuxONE, with explainable risk scores, pseudonymized user IDs, and final decisions kept in human hands.

Tech stack (core)

pandasNumPyscikit-learnjoblibPyYAMLFlaskpytest
System pipeline

One pipeline, five steps

All stages run inside LinuxONE. Steps communicate only through data-contract files — not internal APIs.

01

Ingest & pseudonymize

CERT/LANL loaders ingest multi-source logs; identities are hashed (HMAC-SHA256) right at ingestion.

ingestdata/interim/events.csv.gz · Contract #1
02

Daily behavior features

Per user × day aggregation + deviation (z-score) against each user's own 14-day baseline — leakage-free.

featuresdata/processed/features.csv.gz · Contract #2
03

Train hybrid models

TEMPORAL split: supervised (HistGradientBoosting) + Isolation Forest for novel behavior.

trainmodels/bundle.joblib · Contract #4
04

Alert-budget evaluation

Realistic metrics for rare events: precision/recall @ budget + time-to-detection.

evaluateoutputs/metrics.json · Contract #5
05

Score, explain, decide

Risk score 0–1, per-alert explanation (SHAP/Shapley/deviation), then mapped to the 3-tier policy.

scoreoutputs/alerts.jsonl · Contract #3

Modules inside the repo

Pseudonymization

ingest/pseudonymize.py

HMAC-SHA256 keyed hash (16 hex). The key lives in `.env` and never leaves the instance.

Replay stream

ingest/replay.py

Replays logs as an event stream — honestly declared as a replay, not real-time.

Explanations

models/explain.py

shap → shapley (own sampling, exact efficiency) → deviation. The method used is recorded as-is.

Policy

policy/policy.py

Score → 3 response tiers. The system NEVER blocks accounts automatically.

Case summaries

llm/summarizer.py

Plain-language template (default). Accepts only pseudonymized fields.

API + dashboard

api/app.py

Flask :8000 — /health, /api/alerts, /api/metrics, POST /api/score, alert page.

Container

deploy/Dockerfile

python:3.11-slim (fallback ubi9/python-311). Data & keys are mounted, never baked into the image.

Pipeline CLI

src/trailguard/pipeline.py

`python -m trailguard.pipeline all` — ingest → features → train → evaluate → score.

Working principles

How we work while new to Linux

Five rules that keep the team moving even though the environment is unfamiliar and time is short.

1

Always a working version

`main` must pass `make toy` at any time. Toy data lets every group work in parallel.

2

Data contracts first, code second

Groups communicate only through the agreed Data Contracts (#1–#5).

3

Only claim what actually works

Terms like “SHAP” or “Parquet” are not written until they are proven to run on LinuxONE.

4

Cut scope early

Cut decisions happen at the Gate, not at the end. MoSCoW guides priorities.

5

Everyone passes Linux survival

Every member (not just Group A) completes the basic Linux & LinuxONE checklist first.

Scope priorities · MoSCoW

What is required, what is a stretch

Cut scope early — decisions happen at the Gate, not at the end. The SHAP claim target is judged go/no-go at Gate 1.

MUST

  • Runs on LinuxONE
  • Pseudonymization
  • Daily features
  • Isolation Forest + supervised
  • Risk score
  • 3-tier policy (human approval)
  • Simple dashboard
  • Alert-budget evaluation + time-to-detection
  • Two datasets: CERT + LANL (subset)
  • Shapley-value based explanations (own implementation)

Required to finish

TARGET — the "SHAP" claim

  • Library `shap` runs on s390x
  • pyarrow / Parquet

Go/no-go at Gate 1

SHOULD

  • Container runs
  • Latency/throughput benchmark
  • Baseline comparison in the evaluation
  • LANL: full evaluation with a comparison baseline

Gate 2 / Gate 3

COULD

  • Small LLM for case summaries
  • Live replay with speed control
  • Approve/reject buttons in the dashboard

Gate 3

WON'T

  • Full LANL (1 billion rows, ~7 GB gz) on the VM
  • Deep learning
  • Multi-user authentication

Out of scope

DEFERRED

  • Evidence screenshots
  • Final README
  • Limitations section
  • Demo video
  • Submission

Split after Gate 3

Early decisions already locked in

D1

Flask (not FastAPI/Streamlit)

Pure-Python; avoids pydantic-core/pyarrow, which are risky on s390x.

D2

CSV.gz between steps by default; Parquet optional

pyarrow is risky on s390x; the pipeline falls back automatically with a warning.

D3

Supervised = HistGradientBoostingClassifier (sklearn); fallback GradientBoostingClassifier

No extra dependencies; light enough for LinuxONE. Older sklearn builds (e.g. s390x apt 0.23) lack HGB — the actual model used is recorded in metrics (sup_model).

D4

SHAP is a target claim. Order: shap → shapley → deviation

Claims must match the method that actually ran (explain_method column).

D5

LANL stays in scope as a subset (streaming prefilter)

Full data is not viable on the VM; separate pipeline via config_lanl.yaml.

D6

TEMPORAL split + alert-budget & time-to-detection metrics

Extremely rare data; avoids future leakage.

D7

Replay = stream simulation, honestly declared

A “real-time” claim must be backed by numbers.

Features & model

Daily behavior, two datasets

One row = one user × one day. Every feature has a deviation version (z-score) against that user's own 14-day baseline — never seeing today, so leakage-free.

CERT (insider misuse)

features/builder.py
n_logonn_offhours_logonn_weekend_logonn_distinct_hostn_new_hostn_usb_connectn_file_opsn_httpn_new_domainn_emailn_email_extemail_ext_bytes

12 deviation features auto-derived · 12 base features + 12 deviations (14-day baseline z-score per user).

LANL (stolen credentials)

features/builder_lanl.py
n_authn_failn_logonn_network_logonn_remoten_distinct_dstn_new_dstn_distinct_srcn_new_srcn_night

10 deviation features auto-derived · 10 base features + 10 deviations. `n_night` is only a proxy (LANL timestamps are anonymous).

Split

Temporal (not random) — 65% train / 35% test

Supervised

HistGradientBoostingClassifier + class weights (fallback: GradientBoostingClassifier when HGB is unavailable)

Anomaly

IsolationForest, trained on normal behavior

Score blend

risk = 0.6 · p_supervised + 0.4 · p_anomaly

Evaluation

Alert budget 5/day · precision/recall · median days-to-detection

Results (placeholder). The precision/recall @ budget & median days-to-detection table will be filled by the team once outputs/metrics.json exists — toy numbers must not be reported.

Explainability & honesty

The reason behind each alert, method as-is

Three explanation paths, strongest to fallback. The explain_method column in alerts.jsonl is the single source of truth for claims.

shap

SHAP library

shap.Explainer + model-agnostic. Requires the shap package (numba/llvmlite) — must be tested on s390x first.

shapley

Shapley (own implementation)

Permutation sampling, pure NumPy. Exact efficiency holds: Σ contributions + base = f(x).

deviation

Deviation

Last resort: how far features deviate from the user's usual behavior (z-score).

Honest-claims checklist

ClaimClaimable if…Do not claim if…
Runs on LinuxONEuname/lscpu screenshot showing Architecture: s390xOnly runs on a laptop
"SHAP"explain_method == "shap" in alerts + [OK] shap in shap_pyarrow_check.txtexplain_method == "shapley" → write “Shapley-value explanations (own implementation)”
"Parquet / pyarrow"[OK] pyarrow + io.format: parquet actually usedpyarrow failed / fell back to CSV.gz
"Two datasets"CERT and LANL results from metrics.json / lanl_metrics.jsonClaiming full LANL (1 billion rows) was processed
Privacy-preserving“Reduces exposure through pseudonymization”Claiming formal privacy guarantees / differential privacy
"Near real-time"Per-event latency numbers exist + described as a replayWriting “real-time” without measurement
Policy · human-in-the-loop

Three tiers, humans stay in control

Risk score 0–1 maps to tiered responses. The system never blocks accounts automatically — high-impact actions require analyst approval.

tier 1risk < 0.60

log_only

Log only. No automatic action.

Automatic, no impactful action
tier 20.60 ≤ risk < 0.85

step_up_verification

Request additional verification on the next session.

Automatic, no impactful action
tier 3risk ≥ 0.85

analyst_ticket

Create an analyst ticket; follow-up actions MUST be approved by a human.

Human approval required

Thresholds from configs/config.yaml: step_up_threshold: 0.60 · ticket_threshold: 0.85

Datasets

Two environments, kept separate

CERT (insider misuse) and LANL (stolen credentials) are evaluated separately because their environments differ. LANL is built as a structured subset.

CMU CERT Insider Threat

Primary · synthetic

Multi-source: logon, device, file, http, email (+ LDAP & psychometric).

  • Version r4.2; the answers/ folder marks insiders
  • Large (http.csv especially) — cap it with max_rows_per_file
  • Synthetic → does not represent production networks (say so in Limitations)

LANL Cyber-Security Events

Secondary · subset

De-identified authentication logs (~58 days) + red-team labels.

  • auth.txt.gz ~1 billion rows / ~7 GB gz — do NOT load it fully
  • Streaming prefilter: all red-team victim users + a 2% sample of others
  • Time is anonymous (relative only); very few labels — report as-is

Prefilter streaming:python scripts/prefilter_lanl.py --user-fraction 0.02 --max-day 58

Deployment · IBM LinuxONE

Runs on s390x, containerized

The whole pipeline and dashboard run inside a LinuxONE instance. This static landing is served by nginx on the VM.

s390x platform

LinuxONE Community Cloud. Verify with uname/lscpu: Architecture: s390x.

Container

python:3.11-slim (fallback ubi9/python-311). Data & model are mounted; raw logs & keys never go into the image.

Static nginx

This landing page builds to static files (dist/) and is served by nginx — a natural fit for a LinuxONE VM.

R17 — Node tooling

If npm/build misbehaves on s390x: build on a laptop then copy dist/ to the VM, or serve via Flask.

on the LinuxONE VM
$ bash scripts/00_check_env.sh— check architecture & tools (expect s390x)
$ bash scripts/01_setup_env.sh— venv + dependencies
$ make toy— toy data + full pipeline (< 1 min)
$ make shap-check— go/no-go SHAP & pyarrow
$ make api— dashboard on :8000
$ make container— build & run with podman/docker

Why it is privacy-safe

  • HMAC key lives in .env; raw data & the key do not go into the container image.
  • Identities are hashed at ingestion (HMAC-SHA256, 16 hex) — the dashboard only shows pseudonymized IDs.
  • The model is pickled & loaded on the same architecture (LinuxONE) — train and load on the same machine.
LinuxONE evidence

Judges evaluate through screenshots

All evidence is time/date & hostname stamped and stored in evidence/. Without evidence, a feature is not written as a claim.

01

uname -a + lscpu (Architecture: s390x)

02

free -h, df -h, nproc (VM resources)

03

make run finished on the VM (log & timing)

04

podman/docker ps + curl /health

05

Dashboard (via tunnel) with alerts & tiers

06

metrics.json & benchmark.json

07

top/htop during the benchmark (CPU/memory)

08

Evidence of pseudonymization + .env not in the repo

09

shap_pyarrow_check.txt (claim proof / fallback)

10

LANL subset size & prefilter log

make evidence

Collects system info (uname, lscpu, free, df, ML package versions, containers, latest metrics & benchmarks) into evidence/system_info.txt — then screenshot the screen.

Evidence > claims

A feature that cannot be shown in a screenshot or video is not written as a claim. SHAP only if evidence/shap_pyarrow_check.txt shows [OK] shap.

Team & responsibilities

6 people, 3 groups, clear file ownership

Each group holds 2 different roles that back each other up. Avoid Git conflicts by only editing your own files.

A — Platform & Deploy

A-Platform

LinuxONE environment: SSH, Python, packages, data on the VM, system evidence

A-Deploy

Containers, performance benchmark, Makefile, security evidence

B — Data & Model

B-Data

CERT/LANL loaders, feature building, data quality

B-Model

Hybrid model, tuning, honest evaluation, alert explanations

C — Integration & Product

C-Lead (PM)

Pipeline, pseudonymization, policy, API; keeps Gates & the Decision Log

C-Demo

Dashboard, replay, case summaries, README, video & submission

Branches per role

a-platform/… b-model/… c-lead/… — merge into main via small PRs, reviewed by other groups.

main stays green

Before merging, make toy must succeed. Do not commit large data, .env, or .joblib models.

PM = keeps the Gates

Stand-ups are sent to the PM at every Gate & the LANL Checkpoint; the Decision Log is the project's decision memory.

Stages & Gates

From ready to feature freeze

Each stage starts after the previous Gate/Checkpoint is reached. Work order follows stages & Gates — not the clock.

  1. Stage 0

    Ready

    • A1 SSH + make check (record OS/Python/RAM/disk)
    • B1 download & understand CERT
    • C1 repo, .env, HMAC key
  2. Stage 1

    Foundation

    • A2 make setup / make toy / make lanl-toy
    • A3 go/no-go SHAP & pyarrow
    • C8 start review; read the data contracts
  3. Gate 1

    Foundation proven

    • make toy & make lanl-toy succeed on LinuxONE
    • SHAP & pyarrow decisions recorded
    • Node/npm (React) tests on the VM recorded
  4. Stage 2

    Real data + baseline

    • A5 CERT data to the VM · A11 download+prefilter LANL
    • B2/B3 real CERT loader & features
    • C3a main pages (toy data)
  5. Checkpoint LANL

    LANL subset ready

    • data/raw/lanl_sub/ exists & its size is recorded
    • B-Data can use it
  6. Gate 2

    End-to-end

    • CERT (sample) end-to-end → alerts visible in the dashboard
    • LANL pipeline end-to-end on the subset
  7. Stage 3

    Polish & wire up

    • Container, benchmark, evaluation + comparison
    • Final policy, case summaries, approve/reject
  8. Gate 3

    FEATURE FREEZE

    • After this only bug fixes + deferred work
    • Evidence, documentation, video split (§8)
Risk management

What can break the project

Every risk has a mitigation and an owner. High risks (R1, R8, R9, R11) are tightly guarded through the Gates.

#RiskImpactMitigationOwner
R1ML packages fail to install on s390x (big-endian, no wheels)HighCore stays light (sklearn/pandas/flask). Fallback: HistGradientBoosting, own Shapley / deviationA
R2Scope too largeHighMoSCoW; the Gate decides cutsPM
R3VM limits (RAM/CPU/disk) vs large dataMediumCERT sampling; max_rows_per_file; check free -hA+B
R4SSH drops, processes dieMediumAlways run inside tmuxA
R5Real CERT label/file format differs from toyMediumB adapts loader.py at Stage 2B
R6Not enough LinuxONE evidence laterMediumPeriodic make evidence as archive; screenshot split waits for §8A-Deploy
R7Overclaiming (real-time, SHAP, formal privacy)MediumClaim rules §3b; dashboard shows explain_method as-isC
R8Last-minute integration bugsHighFeature freeze at Gate 3; main always greenPM
R9Keys/tokens leak to GitHubHigh.gitignore, .env never committed, check before pushC-Lead
R10Originality rule violationsFatalSee the Integrity section in 04_SUBMISSION_CHECKLIST.mdEveryone
R11LANL ~7 GB / 1B rows: disk/RAM/time not enoughHighStreaming prefilter; measure --max-lines; check df -h; Checkpoint LANLA-Deploy + B-Data
R12shap/numba/llvmlite cannot be installed → SHAP claim failsMediumGo/no-go at Gate 1; fallback own Shapley; claim follows explain_methodA-Platform + B-Model
R13LANL: few red-team labels & anonymous time → unstable metricsMediumReport positive counts as-is + intervals; do not round awayB-Model
R14api/templates/ conflict—No longer applicable — the whole dashboard is owned by C-Demo—
R17Node/npm or esbuild/rollup problems on s390x, or registry unreachableMediumTest npm install && npm run build at A3b; fallback: build on a laptop, copy dist to the VMA-Platform + C-Demo
R15PM is an AI: does not monitor Discord/Git/VM by itselfMediumStandard stand-up relay per Gate (format §8); Decision Log as memoryC-Lead
R16Unbalanced workload / misestimatesMediumRe-check at Gate 1; move tasks via PM & record in the Decision LogPM
Definition of Done

Done means measurable

The project counts as finished when this list is met — all at the system level (not just a plan).

Definition of Done

  • make toy and make lanl-toy run on LinuxONE
  • CERT (sample) & LANL subset pipelines run end-to-end on LinuxONE
  • make ui builds the React dashboard on the VM
  • Dashboard shows alerts + reasons + tier + approval status; the demo page shows the replay
  • outputs/metrics.json, lanl_metrics.json & benchmark.json contain real numbers from LinuxONE
  • docs/06_ARSITEKTUR_KEAMANAN.md completed
  • main is green (make toy + make lanl-toy pass)

Deferred after Gate 3

No owner yet; discussed together once the system is complete.

  • LinuxONE evidence screenshots and the make evidence archive
  • “Limitations” section (synthetic data, LANL subset & anonymization, label scarcity, leakage risk)
  • Final claim review (match against explain_method & shap_pyarrow_check.txt)
  • Final README
  • Demo video
  • Submission & dry-run (04_SUBMISSION_CHECKLIST.md)
